literal: Purity of mind, purity of action done, both, depending on purity of association, will come.
translation: Purity of mind and purity of action—both of these will arise by depending on the purity of one's association.
modern: மனதின் தூய்மை, செய்யும் செயலின் தூய்மை ஆகிய இரண்டும், ஒருவன் சேரும் இனத்தின் தூய்மையைப் பொறுத்தே உண்டாகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights how deeply our environment and company shape our character and conduct. It states that both internal purity (purity of mind) and external purity (purity of deeds) do not arise in isolation; rather, they are built upon the purity of the association we keep. The word 'tūvā' functions as a participle meaning 'depending upon' or 'resting upon', showing that good company is the foundation of all virtue. Therefore, to keep one's thoughts and actions pure, one must first ensure that their circle of friends and associates is pure.
